title: Household environmental behavior is shaped by dwelling, tenure, proximity, nature contact, and region—not only environmental attitudes or income
source_unit: Statistics Canada, Understanding factors shaping household environmental practices and behaviours in Canada
geography: Canada; analysis of the 2021 Households and the Environment Survey

observations.period: 2021 survey data; publication September 23, 2026; kitchen-waste composting

denominator.unit: Canadian households in the 2021 Households and the Environment Survey; article summary does not state an analytic sample size

overall_composting.unit: percent of households reporting composting kitchen waste

apartment_composting.unit: percent of households in apartments or flats reporting kitchen-waste composting

single_detached_composting.unit: percent of households in single-detached dwellings reporting kitchen-waste composting

renter_composting.unit: percent of renter households reporting kitchen-waste composting

owner_composting.unit: percent of owner households reporting kitchen-waste composting

dwelling_conversion.value: Residential context was more strongly associated with composting than sociodemographic characteristics alone in adjusted models

observations.method: Statistics Canada analysis of 2021 Households and the Environment Survey data, comparing dwelling, tenure, sociodemographic, nature-interaction, and geographic characteristics with multivariate adjustment.
observations.uncertainty: The article reports associations from cross-sectional survey data and does not establish whether dwelling form, service availability, household selection, or local norms causes composting differences.
observations.subgroup: Canadian households by dwelling type, tenure, length of residence, household characteristics, province, and population-area size.
observations.counterinterpretation: Dwelling type may proxy for municipal collection service, storage space, household composition, income, or neighbourhood selection rather than directly causing behavior.

observations.period: 2021 survey data; kitchen-waste composting and proximity to nature

denominator.unit: Canadian households in the 2021 Households and the Environment Survey; analytic sample not disclosed in article summary

nearby_green_space_visit.unit: percent composting among households with access to nearby parks or greenspaces who visited them

no_nearby_green_space_access.unit: percent composting among households reporting no access to nearby parks or greenspaces

plant_growing.unit: percent composting among households growing vegetables, herbs, fruits, flowers, or plants for personal use

no_plant_growing.unit: percent composting among households not growing plants for personal use

nature_practice_link.value: Interaction with nearby nature and household cultivation are associated with higher composting participation

observations.method: Cross-sectional comparison and adjusted models linking household environmental practices with parks, greenspaces, outdoor activity, and personal cultivation.
observations.uncertainty: Nature interaction may reflect housing, community, values, service access, or self-selection; the study does not identify a causal pathway from parks to composting.
observations.subgroup: Canadian households with differing access to nearby greenspace, outdoor activity, gardening, dwelling conditions, and regional context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Composting and nature contact may be jointly produced by local infrastructure or household environmental orientation rather than one causing the other.

denominator.unit: Canadian households reporting hazardous waste in the prior 12 months; article summary does not state analytic sample size

households_with_hazardous_waste.unit: percent of households with hazardous waste to dispose of in the prior 12 months

controlled_disposal_general.unit: approximately percent of households using controlled disposal methods across hazardous-waste categories

e_waste_adults_only.unit: percent of adults-only households using controlled e-waste disposal

e_waste_seniors_only.unit: percent of senior-only households using controlled e-waste disposal

e_waste_single_detached.unit: percent of single-detached households using controlled e-waste disposal

e_waste_apartment.unit: percent of apartment or flat households using controlled e-waste disposal

disposal_infrastructure.value: Controlled disposal varies with household composition and dwelling context, indicating that environmental behavior depends on usable disposal routes

observations.method: Statistics Canada analysis of reported hazardous materials and controlled disposal, including return-to-supplier, depot, drop-off, pharmacy, or medical-sharps programs.
observations.uncertainty: The study measures self-reported disposal practices and does not audit waste streams, municipal capacity, contamination, or environmental outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Households by composition, education, dwelling type, tenure duration, region, and census-metropolitan-area size.
observations.counterinterpretation: Household composition and dwelling differences may reflect age, health, waste types, service access, or knowledge rather than willingness or environmental values alone.

observations.period: 2021 survey data; geographic and settlement-scale variation

denominator.unit: Canadian households in the 2021 Households and the Environment Survey; provincial and census-area comparisons

prince_edward_island_composting.unit: percent of households reporting kitchen-waste composting

nova_scotia_composting.unit: percent of households reporting kitchen-waste composting

newfoundland_labrador_composting.unit: percent of households reporting kitchen-waste composting

large_cma_composting.unit: percent of households in large census metropolitan areas reporting kitchen-waste composting

small_urban_composting.unit: percent of households in small urban areas reporting kitchen-waste composting

place_behavior_gap.value: Environmental household practices vary sharply by province and settlement scale, beyond a simple individual-attitude explanation

observations.method: Descriptive and adjusted geographic comparisons across Canadian provinces and census-metropolitan-area categories.
observations.uncertainty: Geographic differences combine service infrastructure, policy, housing, climate, culture, household composition, and selection; the report does not decompose these causes into a single estimate.
observations.subgroup: Canadian households in provinces, large/medium/small CMAs, small urban areas, and non-urban areas.
observations.counterinterpretation: High or low provincial rates may reflect waste-collection systems or survey reporting differences rather than durable cultural norms.

related_sources.claim: Statistics Canada Economic and Social Reports series and September 2026 issue context.
Households and the Environment Survey programme context.

boundary: This record adds a household-environmental behavior layer: housing form, tenure, residence duration, nearby nature, settlement scale, and disposal infrastructure condition composting and hazardous-waste practices. It uses 2021 Canadian survey data published in 2026; it is not a current causal experiment, a measure of environmental attitudes alone, an audited waste-flow estimate, or proof that household behavior produces environmental outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Statistics Canada article reviewed for release date, 2021 HES frame, composting, dwelling/tenure, nature interaction, hazardous-waste disposal, and geographic estimates.
